narratives.Overview:
Split from #4503 later-arc.

## Pain

After the #4503 Bound-remedy (named `observable-scope-markup-unresolved`, same-both-sides no-op for unresolvable selectedness, revision-scoped import following, import-root list not `policy.surfaces`), the originating consumer scenario is still a false pass:

```tsx
const [tab, setTab] = useState("overview");
<Tabs value={tab} onValueChange={setTab}>
  <TabsTrigger value="overview">Overview</TabsTrigger>
  <TabsTrigger value="billing">Billing</TabsTrigger>
</Tabs>
```

A fields-only PR that also flips `useState("overview")` to `useState("billing")` still prints oracle coverage and exits 0. Both revisions have `value={tab}`. Same-both-sides no-op treats that as unchanged. Always-fail on a controlled `value=` expression hard-fails every PR that touches the file. Seeing the flip as a `tab-selected` delta is flow analysis on a mutable binding.

## What this is not

- Not #4495 first-ship.
- Not the #4503 subset (uncontrolled `defaultValue={DEFAULT_TAB}` / in-file const / imported `.ts` constant as a revision-scoped witness, plus the named throw token).
- Not jsdom / screenshots / executing consumer source.

## Origin

#4503 later-arc Stop 1 restated P1 as a false pass. Cap-3 pain-audit 5687959987 refused relief: fail-closed without a token is a no-op; the throw is unshippable as surface-wide; conditioning on the change leaves this scenario silent. Recut 5687984715 records that split. This issue is the leftover carrier.

## Method

Re-verified anchors; line cites are not evidence.

- `git show` of `packages/core/src/observable-scope/extract.ts` (isTab, jsxSelected, jsxAttr), `evaluate.ts` (coverage return, markup-unresolved routing), `extract.test.ts` (committed "not state expressions" case), `diff.ts` (set-difference), `types.ts` (4503 leftover comment).

- `Tabs` `value={tab}` is `jsxAttr` kind `expr`, identifier `tab`, identical across revisions.

## Mechanism inventory

How this module can stop exit 0 today:

| Channel | Result |
| --- | --- |
| throw `observable-scope-markup-unresolved` (parse5 anomalies / TS parseDiagnostics only) | `fail`, code 1, before mint, unwaivable |
| throw parser-unresolvable / parser-invalid | `config`, code 2 |
| fact-id set-difference the mint did not list | `fail`, code 1, waivable by `allowedChanges` |
| `mustPreserve` hit | `fail`, code 1 |
| matched UI, no merge-base mint | `fail`, code 1 |

There is no third state. Identical fact lists, including two empty lists, take the coverage `ok()`: "minted allowedChanges cover the parse5+typescript oracle". `jsxAttr` already classifies a non-literal as `expr` and then drops it. `visitJsx` already walks the whole source file; VariableDeclarations are in that tree and are currently ignored. No identifier resolver, no callee unwrap, no `value=` selectedness, no `TabsTrigger` tag.

Always-fail on a controlled `value=` expression would reuse the existing markup-unresolved channel. That channel returns before mint is read. Keep that rejection.

## Findings

### F1 -- `blocks-the-design`

**The write-back closes the originating witness by calling it flow analysis. It is not.**

Evidence: the probe. `tab` is a `const` binding. Mutations in this snippet go through `setTab`, which a parse-only oracle already refuses to run. The PR under discussion changes the `useState` *argument*, a `StringLiteral` on a CallExpression that is the initializer of that const. `jsxAttr` already returns `{ kind: "expr", text: "tab" }` for `value={tab}` and that node is identical on both revisions. The shipped "not state expressions" test is `<Tab selected={isOn}>`, a different node: selectedness as an identifier *on the tab*, not an initializer behind a root `value=`.

Failure mode: bind this dichotomy and P1 has no remaining mechanism. A builder either waives the originating consumer scenario (coverage line, exit 0, forever) or ships a walker this issue has classified as out of contract. A leftover *work* issue cannot bind as an unsolvable class when the originating change is a string literal in an already-parsed TSX file.

Disposition consequence: drop the flow-analysis close. Remaining mechanism, using inventory rather than a new oracle: if `value={ident}` and `ident` is the first element of `const [ident, ...] = useState(<StringLiteral>)` in the same file, emit `tab-selected` from the matching `TabsTrigger value=` literal. Closed callee names (`useState`, `React.useState`). Non-literal args, lazy `() =>`, and `setTab` stay unresolvable. That is one callee unwrap on a const initializer, the same static class as an in-file const, not reaching definitions.

### F2 -- `sharpens-framing`

**Stop 1 records pain and two closed doors. It does not name a remaining mechanism.**

Evidence: comment 5689608002. P1, always-fail rejected, flow analysis rejected, no Bound-remedy, no token, no unwrap, no test surface. The issue body lists #4503 Bound-remedy parts (`observable-scope-markup-unresolved` for unresolvable selectedness, same-both-sides, revision-scoped follow, import-root ≠ `policy.surfaces`). Those strings are absent from `packages/core/src/observable-scope/*.ts` at `f2590baf`. #4503 is still open. `types.ts` and `content/docs/observable-scope.md` still point runtime default-tab at #4503.

Failure mode: an all-accept map over this write-back harvests an empty next-build. A worker on master would not find the mechanisms the body says this leftover sits *after*.

Disposition consequence: name F1's unwrap as the next-build, or cancel this number if that unwrap is taken as a clause on #4503's resolve axis. Do not bind a pain-only body. Do not implement the #4503 recognizer / follow / same-both-sides set from this issue.

### F3 -- `sharpens-framing`

**At this SHA the scenario is silent for two reasons; only one is this leftover.**

Evidence: probe `TabsTrigger` `isTab=false`. git-shown `isTab` is `role="tab"` / `Tab` / `Tabs.Tab` only. After a recognizer that treats `TabsTrigger` as a tab and `Tabs value=` as the selectedness root, shipped facts would still match across the flip (`tab:Overview`, `tab:Billing`, no `tab-selected`) because `value={tab}` does not change. That second silence is P1. The first silence is the #4503 recognizer, not this issue.

Failure mode: implementing 4586 first re-builds the recognizer and races open #4503. Implementing 4586 as if the recognizer already shipped fails on this dest.

Disposition consequence: this number is after the #4503 recognizer, not beside it. The unwrap in F1 is the leftover. Keep `TabsTrigger` / `defaultValue` / import-follow off this next-build.

### F4 -- `footnote`

`changeKind` is stored and never read by `evaluate.ts`; `parseAllowed` accepts `tab-selected` under `fields-only`. Relevant only if F1 produces a selection delta. Recorded so a mint cannot silently waive that delta with a kind-wide allow.

### F5 -- `footnote`

The HTML parity corpus file `page-10.html` contains the word `useState` because it is a scraped React docs page. It is not a fixture for this carrier.

## Injection / swarm lens

Fires on untrusted input, low altitude. F1's unwrap reads CallExpression arguments and array-binding names inside TSX the extractor already parses. Closed callee. Same file. Parse-only. No new import graph, worktree, identity, or prompt surface. Unknown callee or non-literal arg stays unresolvable; if #4503 later no-ops an identically unresolvable site, that no-op still applies. Do not execute `useState`. Do not walk `setTab`.

## Road not taken

I considered grading this as an honest unsolvable leftover: the selection *attribute* is identical, same-both-sides is the right no-op, always-fail is unshippable, park the issue.

Rejected because the originating PR does not need the attribute to change. It changes the initializer of the const that identifier names. Parking that would waive the write-back's own scenario.

## Steelman

The strongest case for the flow-analysis close: React state is a snapshot; `setTab` in an effect or handler can make the runtime selected tab differ from the `useState` argument, so treating the argument as `tab-selected` is a lie about runtime. The oracle is committed source versus committed source, not jsdom. The write-back's own scenario is the argument flip, which is on the page as a `StringLiteral`. Effects and handlers are a later hole; they are not this P1.

What would flip F1: the originating snippet using `useState(() => ...)`, `useState(props.tab)`, or a `let` that is assigned before the JSX. Those are unresolvable. The posted snippet is not.

## Verdict

P1 is real: a fields-only PR that flips `useState("overview")` to `useState("billing")` on this snippet produces no shipped fact delta, so the coverage line is the empty-leftover path. Always-fail on `value=` expressions stays rejected. The flow-analysis close does not hold, and without it this write-back has no named remaining mechanism and is not independently implementable at this SHA. The lean cannot bind as written.

## Census

5 findings: 1 `blocks-the-design` (F1), 2 `sharpens-framing` (F2, F3), 2 `footnote` (F4, F5). EXIT after this post.
